requirement_coverage.reason: No authoritative complete product requirement/AC inventory was supplied.

execution_case_denominator.reason: Scenario groups are not executable cases. Exact case/layer/input/oracle/evidence mappings must be frozen before execution metrics.

denominators.calculation: Count unique declared proposal projects and scenario-group IDs; never derive product requirements or approved runnable cases from these counts.

policies.denominator_changes: New or removed projects/groups require a new inventory version and an explicit changelog; preserve the previous snapshot.
policies.results: Retain original source/candidate/environment/run bindings. An observation without an exact mapping is not promoted into a scenario result.
policies.negative_cases: Record observed product verdict separately from the independent expected-detection evaluation. Expected failure detection does not turn the product verdict into PASS.
policies.no_layer_promotion: Upstream/client/helper success does not imply native provider, module, native Swarm-agent or SIT success.
policies.artifact_policy: Link authorized immutable artifacts and hashes. Local/Cloud paths are locations only, not download links. Never publish private logs, secrets or holdouts.
policies.maintenance: Update scenario layer_results only with frozen executable case IDs, input/oracle review pins, actual runtime version, canonical run ID, validated evidence and review references.
policies.source_ownership: Cross-repository SIT suites belong under tests/sit/ in an existing product repository. Unit, local and other integration tests retain their owning repository's conventions and paths. Product Knowledge repositories own governed knowledge/traceability; Cognee is a retrieval index. This tool-repository inventory records validation of the tooling itself.
policies.exclusions: Do not remove blocked or unsupported groups. Any approved exclusion must retain ID, reason, authority/review reference and inventory version.
policies.reusable_flows: Authoring/compiler work is DEFERRED until repeated real flows across at least two repositories justify it; no new DSL is inferred from this planning inventory.

status_reasons.NOT_RECONCILED: The source observation has not been mapped to a frozen exact scenario/case/layer/input/oracle/run.
status_reasons.NOT_RUN: No execution is established for this candidate or native-agent layer in the proposal.
status_reasons.BLOCKED: A required runtime/admission/access prerequisite is missing. Project blockers and the reference-version support boundary explain the affected group.

policies.historical_scenario_classification: Historical slot is preserved raw metadata, not an authoritative scenario category. Records explicitly normalized as PIN_MISMATCH do not establish dependency-outage coverage. Do not infer the admission/execution stage without underlying evidence.
policies.capability_status_dimensions: Capability layer_results.state and reconciliation_state describe reconciliation only. linked_group_status_summary reports declared states of uniquely counted scenario groups from proposed project links; it is not a capability execution verdict, readiness decision, approved mapping or a new denominator. execution_started is UNKNOWN unless independently established; NOT_RUN and BLOCKED do not establish whether an execution was attempted.

component_plan.original_component_markdown:
# Major component coverage gap matrix

Snapshot: 2026-11-07 UTC. Supplements the existing 20-repository planning inventory; does not silently replace its project/scenario denominators. Read-only source/evidence review, no new installation, test, deployment or infrastructure operation.

## Conclusion

The 20 repositories are not sufficient to establish coverage of the user's main technology stack. They emphasize gRPC and Python clients. A repository can mention a dependency without that dependency or its integration being tested. Use capability × scenario × implementation version × execution layer × environment, not repository count, as the acceptance matrix.

## Capability inventory (17 proposed acceptance categories, no aggregate PASS claimed)

| ID | Capability | Current evidence in this work | Missing acceptance / next slice | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | REST / HTTP | Product/application candidates include FastAPI, Petclinic, eShop, Gitea, etc.; no complete per-capability acceptance shown by this inventory | method/status/header/schema, pagination, auth/authorization, idempotency, timeout/retry, app→DB/MQ full path | P0 |
| C02 | gRPC | Original two project probes; isolated Java patch regression 98 JUnit tests; new expansion wire-results has 12 passing rows for Node/interceptor/betterproto | method/cardinality/schema admissions, binary/duplicate/trailer metadata, deadline/cancellation, exact status; current framework/module/native agent/SIT pins | P0 |
| C03 | Kafka | Latest broker-results.json has actual aiokafka→Kafka 3.9.2, null/empty/binary keys, headers/tombstone, ordering/count, negative and recovery assertions | framework/module native route, group/rebalance/offset semantics beyond bounded fixture, security/TLS, retry/idempotency, cleanup; no exactly-once delivery guarantee inferred | P0 |
| C04 | NATS | Latest same file has nats.py→NATS 2.10.26, binary/empty/order/count, no responder, invalid/oversize, recovery and closed-client assertions | current framework/module path, complete request/reply and JetStream ack/redelivery/durable semantics, security/TLS, persistence/cleanup | P0 |
| C05 | IBM MQ | Absent from the 20-repo inventory; official sample and chart sources verified now | real queue manager put/get, pub/sub, request/reply correlation, syncpoint commit/backout, DLQ/redelivery, reconnect, queue cleanup | P0 |
| C06 | Oracle | No real Oracle server PASS demonstrated here | actual selected Oracle version + JDBC: bind/NULL/type handling, commit/rollback/savepoint, SQL error codes, stored procedure/cursor where used, timeout, schema cleanup | P0 |
| C07 | IBM Db2 | No real Db2 server PASS demonstrated here | actual selected Db2 platform/version + JDBC/CLI: parameters/types, transaction/isolation, SQLSTATE/SQLCODE, stored procedure where used, connection recovery, schema cleanup | P0 |
| C08 | MariaDB | Real MariaDB 11.8.8 + PyMySQL; module→framework→CLI bridge; newest SQLAlchemy six ORM cases reported PASS | native provider integration, auth/TLS, broader types/transactions, exact version constraints; ORM postrun grading pending | P0 |
| C09 | MongoDB | Real MongoDB 7.0.16 + PyMongo; CLI bridge; newest MongoEngine six ORM cases reported PASS | native provider integration, auth/TLS, replica-set transactions/read concern where applicable, error/recovery/cleanup; ORM postrun grading pending | P0 |
| C10 | MinIO / S3-compatible object storage | 20-repo inventory has no dedicated MinIO case set; SIT worker has not observed actual MinIO API evidence. The 235-byte Kimi text/base64 transport round-trip is not MinIO | actual approved MinIO server + SDK: put/get/list/stat/delete, byte checksum, multipart/abort, presigned URL expiry, forbidden access, retries, bucket/prefix cleanup | P0 |
| C11 | Redis / RESP | Mentioned as dependency of Online Boutique/eShop, not dedicated verification | RESP2/RESP3 shapes, binary/NULL, TTL/expiry, atomic/transaction behavior, reconnect, persistence where used, key-prefix cleanup | P0 |

### IBM MQ

Use ibm-messaging/mq-dev-patterns for real vendor put/get, pub/sub and request/response examples. Its Apache-2.0 sample code is community-supported and requires an actual MQ server with queues/topics. Kafka, NATS, RabbitMQ and a generic mock are not IBM MQ substitutes.

The official sample mq-helm chart at b49fd79e is chart14.0.0, appVersion10.0.1.0, kubeVersion>=1.29.0-0. Its developer image defaults are development-only; Native HA entitlement and other licensed uses must be verified. Do not silently upgrade the user's existing queue manager/chart to this observed source version.

### Oracle and Db2

Oracle samples README states Apache-2.0, but database binaries and distribution agreements are separate. oracle/docker-images is official container build/config source (UPL-1.0); it does not make the Oracle database engine unrestricted open-source software. Choose the user's authorized version/edition, JDBC driver and database before execution.

IBM/db2-samples is Apache-2.0 sample code; sample availability varies by platform/language. Db2 LUW, Db2 for z/OS and Db2 for i are not interchangeable validation targets. Backend version/platform/driver and authorized fixture remain open inputs. H2 compatibility mode, mocked JDBC, unavailable-endpoint tests, and other SQL engines do not establish Oracle/Db2 behavior PASS.

### MinIO

GitHub marks both minio/minio and minio/operator archived. The pinned minio/minio README explicitly says the repository is no longer maintained, community distribution is source-only, and historical binaries are unmaintained. Preserve the user's approved server/chart/image version, validate license/security support, and do not recommend an unqualified latest install.

minio/minio-go remains active and provides S3 APIs suitable for client cases. Its public play server is not a destination for user/SIT data; use an authorized owned endpoint. Passing SDK tests against another S3-compatible service does not prove MinIO-specific behavior.

Archived source chart references: minio/minio chart5.4.0 has appVersion RELEASE.2024-12-18T13-15-44Z; minio/operator chart7.1.1 requires Kubernetes1.30+ per README. These are reference constraints, not recommendations for production or evidence of compatibility with the current K3s.

### Redis

Use redis/redis-py plus the actual approved Redis server/version. The current source supports explicit RESP2/RESP3 selection; pin protocol and response-shape mode. GitHub returns NOASSERTION for server license and the current unstable source needs a large modern build toolchain. Select a supported released server version with matching licensing, not the observed unstable HEAD as a default.

### Helm: separate local checks from actual cluster lifecycle

Official source candidates: nats-io/k8s (chart2.15.2/appVersion2.15.2 at the observed pin) and ibm-messaging/mq-helm (chart14.0.0/appVersion10.0.1.0). NATS chart/app version differs from the already tested local NATS2.10.26; the local broker result cannot validate that chart/image combination. Include the user's actual product chart source as a third subject once its repo/path/version is supplied or found.

- H01 local: Chart.yaml/lock/dependency source, chart archive hash, image digest, kubeVersion and required tool versions.
- H02 local: helm lint; values normal/invalid/boundary sets; JSON schema rejection where schema exists.
- H03 local: helm template output with fixed inputs and controlled random/time/lookup sources; required resource fields, service ports, labels, probes, requests/limits and RBAC. Do not assume every chart renders deterministically.
- H04 local: dependencies/subcharts/conditional resources; Secret references without exposing secret values.
- H05 local: render against target Kubernetes versions; this is not an API-server validation PASS.
- H06 K8s SIT: install in owned namespace; release status, readiness and post-install application protocol tests.
- H07 K8s SIT: upgrade from pinned N to N+1; verify application and data invariants.
- H08 K8s SIT: controlled failure and rollback; verify resources, app version and data separately. Helm rollback is not a database migration rollback guarantee.
- H09 K8s SIT: helm test or explicitly authored post-deploy tests, hook ordering and hook-failure retention.
- H10 K8s SIT: PVC/StorageClass, config/secret references, ingress/service DNS and actual network access.
- H11 K8s SIT: uninstall/cleanup scoped by release+namespace+run_id; retained PVCs/CRDs/hook resources are recorded, never blindly purged.
- H12 evidence: chart/app/image/values/cluster pins, ordered commands, exit statuses, rendered manifests, release history, Kubernetes events/pod logs, protocol results, cleanup receipts.

### Ansible: local checks are not VM acceptance

Use the actual product playbooks/roles with ansible/ansible and ansible/molecule as tooling. The observed ansible source is devel, so select a released ansible-core/toolchain version matched to the real playbooks; Molecule supports the latest two major Ansible versions. Molecule can target containers, VMs or APIs, but a container driver run does not establish VM behavior.

- A01 local: syntax, inventory parsing, group/host targeting, variable precedence, missing/invalid variables, secret redaction.
- A02 target-environment rehearsal, separately authorized: check/diff on supported modules. This is not a pure local static check: it can contact targets, evaluate lookups, and encounter tasks that override check mode. It does not prove commands, service changes or migrations ran.
- A03 actual VM: exact OS/image/architecture, SSH host identity, authorized user/become scope, prerequisite and package state.
- A04 actual VM: deploy pinned package/config; handlers and service start; post-deploy API/DB/MQ test.
- A05 actual VM: second converge unchanged (changed=0, with reviewed documented exceptions); verify resulting state, not just Ansible counters.
- A06 actual VM: change config/version then converge; handlers fire correctly; no unrelated host/resource changes.
- A07 actual VM: controlled task/dependency failure, partial-state evidence, rescue/recovery/rerun or approved rollback.
- A08 actual VM: reboot/reconnect and persistent service/data behavior where applicable.
- A09 actual VM: owned test data and temporary resources cleaned, infrastructure retained/deleted only under agreed scope.
- A10 evidence: playbook/role/collection/inventory/vars hashes (no secrets), controller and VM pins, task events/recap, independent post-deploy observations, first/second-run comparison, recovery/cleanup receipts.

### External systems and shared SIT data

WireMock provides HTTP mock contracts; Toxiproxy provides TCP fault conditions. Both are auxiliary fixtures, not proof of real external-system compatibility. For real integration, name the target, exact interface/spec/version, authenticated test identity, authorized data, expected side effects and cleanup boundary. Add async callback, stale/duplicate/missing event and correlation checks. Controlled outages apply only to owned test fixtures, not shared external services.

Shared data must have an authoritative owner and version; deterministic seed and independently frozen expected output; unique run/tenant/schema/key-prefix/queue/bucket namespace; concurrency/lease policy; prereq ready markers; cross-service referential invariants; reset/reseed; idempotent cleanup after success/failure/timeout/cancel; retained evidence for incomplete cleanup. Do not default to shared-db truncate, bucket purge or cluster-wide delete.

## Priority sequence

1. Freeze C01–C17 capability rows, owners and acceptance boundaries. Locate current product Helm chart and Ansible playbooks; bind exact versions. Prepare Oracle/Db2/MQ licenses, versions and isolated backend prerequisites in parallel.
2. Run small reviewed local slices first: existing gRPC/MQ/DB source cases through actual framework/module paths; Helm lint/template; Ansible syntax/inventory; Redis/MinIO contracts against owned fixtures. No need to wait for full SIT for work that genuinely runs locally.
3. Run IBM MQ/Oracle/Db2 actual vendor fixtures, then real K8s Helm and VM Ansible lifecycles. Reuse exact pins and data contracts, preserving local versus environment results.
4. Finish necessary cross-service and external-system SIT paths, including errors/recovery, teardown and native Swarm actor evidence. Do not infer this from upstream or deployment success alone.

Additional technologies already implied by candidates need explicit acceptance before claiming them: PostgreSQL (Bank/FastAPI/eShop), RabbitMQ/AMQP (eShop), WebSocket (Mattermost). Cross-cutting TLS/mTLS, authentication/authorization, certificates, secrets redaction, timeouts/retries/idempotency, logs/metrics/traces are required per applicable capability. SOAP, SFTP, SMTP and other protocols are applicability candidates, not automatically in scope absent product requirements.

checks.title: Chart.yaml/lock/dependency source, chart archive hash, image digest, kubeVersion and required tool versions.
helm lint; values normal/invalid/boundary sets; JSON schema rejection where schema exists.

helm template output with fixed inputs and controlled random/time/lookup sources; required resource fields, service ports, labels, probes, requests/limits and RBAC. Do not assume every chart renders deterministically.
dependencies/subcharts/conditional resources; Secret references without exposing secret values.
render against target Kubernetes versions; this is not an API-server validation PASS.
install in owned namespace; release status, readiness and post-install application protocol tests.
upgrade from pinned N to N+1; verify application and data invariants.
controlled failure and rollback; verify resources, app version and data separately. Helm rollback is not a database migration rollback guarantee.
helm test or explicitly authored post-deploy tests, hook ordering and hook-failure retention.
PVC/StorageClass, config/secret references, ingress/service DNS and actual network access.
uninstall/cleanup scoped by release+namespace+run_id; retained PVCs/CRDs/hook resources are recorded, never blindly purged.
chart/app/image/values/cluster pins, ordered commands, exit statuses, rendered manifests, release history, Kubernetes events/pod logs, protocol results, cleanup receipts.
syntax, inventory parsing, group/host targeting, variable precedence, missing/invalid variables, secret redaction.

check/diff on supported modules. This is not a pure local static check: it can contact targets, evaluate lookups, and encounter tasks that override check mode. It does not prove commands, service changes or migrations ran.
exact OS/image/architecture, SSH host identity, authorized user/become scope, prerequisite and package state.
deploy pinned package/config; handlers and service start; post-deploy API/DB/MQ test.
second converge unchanged (changed=0, with reviewed documented exceptions); verify resulting state, not just Ansible counters.
change config/version then converge; handlers fire correctly; no unrelated host/resource changes.
controlled task/dependency failure, partial-state evidence, rescue/recovery/rerun or approved rollback.
reboot/reconnect and persistent service/data behavior where applicable.
owned test data and temporary resources cleaned, infrastructure retained/deleted only under agreed scope.
playbook/role/collection/inventory/vars hashes (no secrets), controller and VM pins, task events/recap, independent post-deploy observations, first/second-run comparison, recovery/cleanup receipts.

notes: Original source claims are attributed observations; importing them does not verify execution or acceptance.
H01–H12 and A01–A10 are canonical supplement IDs, distinct from product A01–A09 IDs; qualify references with component_plan.checks.
Molecule container runs do not prove VM behavior; Helm rollback does not prove database rollback.
No approval to deploy derives from this plan.
